title: Present Subjunctive
description: Learn to conjugate and use the present subjunctive mood for uncertainty, doubt, and will in Spanish.

grammar.title: Present Subjunctive Formation
grammar.content:
Present Subjunctive is formed by removing -ar/-er/-ir and adding opposite endings:

For -AR verbs: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -eis, -en

Hablar → Haya, hayas, haja, hablemos, hablEis, hablen

Para -ER/-IR verbs: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -ais, -an

Comer → Coma, comas, coma, comamos, comais, coman
Vivir → Viva, vivas, viva, vivamos, vivais, vivan

Irregular in subjunctive:

Ser → Sea, seas, sea, seamos, seais, sean
Ir → Vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayais, van
Tener → Tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengais, tengan
Hacer → Haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagais, hagan
Venir → Venga, vengas, venga, vengamos, vengais, vengan
Poder → Pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podais, puedan
Querer → Quiera, quieras, quiera, queramos, querais, quieran
Saber → Sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepais, sepan

Decir → Diga, digas, diga, digamos, digais, digan
Ver → Vea, veas, vea, veamos, veais, vean
Dar → Dé, des, dé, demos, deis, den
examples: Espero que vengas a la fiesta. (I hope you come to the party.)
Dudo que ellos sepan la verdad. (I doubt they know the truth.)
Es necesario que hable espanol. (It's necessary that he speak Spanish.)
Quiero que hagas la tarea. (I want you to do the homework.)

grammar.title: When to Use Subjunctive
grammar.content:
Use subjunctive when the main clause expresses:

1. WILL/WISH (querer, necesitar, preferir, esperar):
Quiero que vengas. (I want you to come.)
Espero que tengas suerte. (I hope you have luck.)

2. DOUBT/UNCERTAINTY (dudar, no creer, es posible):
Dudo que llueva manana. (I doubt it rains tomorrow.)
No creo que este aqui. (I don't think he's here.)

3. EMOTION (temer, tener miedo, alegrarse, sentir):
Me alegra que estes aqui. (I'm glad you're here.)
Tengo miedo que llegue tarde. (I'm afraid he'll arrive late.)

4. IMPERSONAL EXPRESSIONS (es importante, es necesario, es logico):
Es importante que estudies. (It's important that you study.)
Es posible que vaya al cine. (It's possible I go to the cinema.)

INDICATIVE (not subjunctive):
When you BELIEVE something is true:
Creo que viene manana. (I believe he's coming tomorrow.) — facts

SUBJUNCTIVE (doubt/unreality):
Dudo que venga manana. (I doubt he's coming tomorrow.)
examples: Creo que tienes razon. (I think you're right.) — fact, use indicative
Dudo que tengas razon. (I doubt you have right.) — doubt, use subjunctive
Es probable que llueva. (It's probable that it rains.) — uncertainty
No creo que sea verdad. (I don't think it's true.) — negation + subjunctive

grammar.title: Subjunctive with Conjunctions
grammar.content:
Subjunctive is used after certain conjunctions when the action is uncertain or future:

1. PURPOSE: para que (so that), con el fin de que
Te doy el libro para que lo leas. (I give you the book so that you read it.)

2. CONTINGENCY: en caso de que (in case), siempre que (as long as)
En caso de que llueva, no saldremos. (In case it rains, we won't go out.)

3. NEGATIVE PURPOSE: sin que (without)
Salio sin que la vieramos. (He left without us seeing him.)

4. TEMPORAL: antes de que (before), hasta que (until)
Llegaremos antes de que llegue ella. (We'll arrive before she arrives.)

5. UNCERTAIN CONDITIONS: como (if/however), donde (where)
Donde quieras que vayas, te encontrare. (Wherever you go, I'll find you.)

INDICATIVE after these conjunctions when the action is CERTAIN/PAST:
Te llamo cuando llegues. (I'll call you when you arrive.) — future uncertainty
Te llame cuando llegaste. (I called you when you arrived.) — past completed
examples: Para que aprendas, tienes que estudiar. (So that you learn, you have to study.)
En caso de que no venga, dejare un mensaje. (In case he doesn't come, I'll leave a message.)
Antes de que salgas, apaga las luces. (Before you leave, turn off the lights.)
Hasta que no llegues, no me ire. (Until you arrive, I won't leave.)

pronunciation.title: Present Subjunctive Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Subjunctive endings have different vowel sounds than indicative:

-AR verbs take -er sounds:
hable → AH-bleh (like indicative 'habla' but with 'e' ending)

-ER/-IR verbs take -ar sounds:
coma → KOH-mah (like indicative 'como' but with 'a' ending)

Key differences:

HABLAR:
Indicative: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablais, hablan
Subjunctive: hable, hables, hable, hablemos, hableis, hablen

COMER:
Indicative: como, comes, come, comemos, comeis, comen
Subjunctive: coma, comas, coma, comamos, comais, coman

Note: The stressed syllable changes position!

Irregulars:
ser → sea (SEH-ah)
ir → vaya (BAH-yah)
tener → tenga (TEHN-gah)
hacer → haga (AH-gah)
examples: hable = AH-bleh (subjunctive, stressed differently than indicative)
coma = KOH-mah (subjunctive, opposite vowel from indicative)

exercises.question: What is the present subjunctive of 'hablar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: Present subjunctive yo of hablar is 'hable'. -AR verbs take -er endings in subjunctive.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Espero que tu ___ a la fiesta. (I hope you come to the party.)'
exercises.explanation: Vengas = you come (subjunctive of venir). After 'espero que', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'I want you to do the homework'?
options: Quiero que tu haces la tarea
Quiero que tu hagas la tarea
Quiero que tu haz la tarea
Quiero que tu harias la tarea
exercises.explanation: 'Quiero que hagas la tarea' uses subjunctive 'hagas' after 'quiero que'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Es necesario que el ___ espanol. (It's necessary that he speak Spanish.)'
exercises.explanation: Hable = he speak (subjunctive of hablar). After 'es necesario que', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I doubt that she knows'?
exercises.explanation: 'Dudo que ella sepa' uses subjunctive 'sepa' after 'dudar'. Doubt triggers subjunctive.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me alegra que tu ___ aqui. (I'm glad you are here.)'
exercises.explanation: Estes = you are (subjunctive of estar). After expressions of emotion, use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses subjunctive correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Es importante que el trabaje' uses subjunctive 'trabaje' after 'es importante'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Dudo que ellos ___ la verdad. (I doubt they know the truth.)'
exercises.explanation: Sepan = they know (subjunctive of saber). After 'dudar', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: What is the subjunctive of 'ser' for 'nosotros'?
exercises.explanation: Seamos = we are (subjunctive of ser). 'Espero que seamos amigos' = I hope we are friends.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Quiero que tu ___ mas cuidado. (I want you to be more careful.)'
exercises.explanation: Tengas = you have (subjunctive of tener). 'Quiero que tengas cuidado' = I want you to be careful.
